To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the porosity REV is typically smaller than CT image sizes, (2) the SW and AI REVS cannot be estimated for cases containing heterogeneous SW distributions, and (3) the SW and the AI REVs are overestimated, due to inherent problems in REV estimation.

(1) estimated porosity REVs are <8 mm3 and smaller than typical CT measurement volumes, (2) SW and AI REV estimation was unsuccessful for cases with heterogeneous SW distributions, and (3) excluding data from non-REV cases can introduce bias into AI-SW relationships.

(1) the requirement of achieving an REV has become a de facto criterion for demonstrating the data quality of CT measurements of porous media properties and (2) this criterion is overly restrictive and may result in the exclusion of data that would be useful for understanding the behavior of porous media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of CT data and how this quality is affected by the requirement of achieving an REV.
the data quality implications associated with a requirement to achieve an REV.
the quality of CT data and the efficient use and analysis of such data, rather than with the quality of a specific CT scanner or image acquisition process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a porosity REV is a useful concept to ensure data quality, but that SW and AI REVS are not useful for ensuring data quality and should not be used as a basis for excluding CT data.
the concept of an REV is not applicable to CT data, but the quality of CT data can still be assessed by examining random fluctuations of data measured over increasing measurement windows.

the data quality implications for the requirement of a REV for CT measurements of porosity and SW in unsaturated porous materials are minimal, whereas the data quality implications associated with the use of REVs for CT measurements of AI are significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of REVs for CT data quality assurance in unsaturated porous systems is not warranted and should be avoided.
the requirement of an estimated REV for CT data quality is problematic, as it may lead to exclusion of data that is not necessarily of low quality.
a porosity REV is necessary but not sufficient, and that SW and AI REV are unnecessary for the reliable estimation of AI-SW relationships.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the requirement of achieving an REV is a poor criterion for assessing data quality.
the data quality implications associated with the REV requirement should be carefully considered when using CT data for quantitative analysis of unsaturated porous media systems.
the requirement for a REV is not a useful criterion for assessing CT data quality in unsaturated porous systems.
